newsitem.title: PERU: Thirty-three confirmed dead in Peru mudslide.
newsitem.headline: Thirty-three confirmed dead in Peru mudslide.

text.p: Thirty-three people were confirmed dead and at least 100 others were missing after a massive mudslide early on Tuesday in Peru's southeastern Andean region of Apurimac, local officials said.

"We have recovered 33 bodies at this point. That is confirmed. Seventeen have been officially registered and another 16 are waiting to be transported and identified," Luis Barra Pacheco, mayor of Abancay, the capital of Apurimac, told Reuters. "Under the mud, there are at least 100 people."
A wall of mud slammed into the villages of Ccocha and Pumaranra in the mountainous region of Apurimac at around 4 a.m. (0900 GMT).
Rescuers at the site told Reuters they had pulled out dozens of bodies from the mud and had seen many more corpses.

"There were arms, heads, pieces of bodies sticking out of the mud," firefighter Richard Rojas told Reuters by telephone soon after returning to Abancay from the site. "We have tried to dig up the bodies using picks and shovels, but it's been difficult."
Rescuers said the corpses had been battered and mutilated by stones carried in the mudslide.
